reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address TiVNbTa, W additions, precipitate formation, or thermal conductivity. E1 discusses strain-rate and temperature effects in NbTaTiV, and E2 discusses general requirements for plasma-facing materials, providing no specific support for the key premises.
premises: TiVNbTa is a single-phase BCC alloy with ~800 MPa yield strength at RT and ~330 MPa at 1273 K
Adding W to TiVNbTa will form coherent W-rich precipitates in a BCC matrix
W-rich nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion at elevated temperatures, improving yield strength retention
The dual-phase microstructure will preserve room-temperature ductility (~40% strain)
The intervention will not degrade thermal conductivity required for heat transfer
